experiment.name: 20260906-llm-decides-on-llm-claims-full-procedure-r2
experiment.question: The architecture minus the solver: LLM-extracted claims, decide prompt with the full procedure. Cheap grid x 10.
experiment.notes:
Re-run of 20260906-llm-decides-on-llm-claims-full-procedure after two runner fixes, with the prompt wording unchanged. (1) The pydantic docstring of DecideResponse ('steps come before outcome so the model reasons before it decides') was being sent to every provider as the JSON-schema 'description'; Claude Fable 5.1's safety classifier refused 57/60 llm-only calls as reasoning_extraction because of it (verified 6 Sep 20:30: with the description dropped the identical prompt passes 3/3; with it, prose or structured justification variants were refused as well). strict_json_schema now drops 'description' for every provider (Gemini and DeepSeek previously received the raw pydantic schema). (2) GPT-5.6's implicit cache breakpoint sits at the end of the whole user message, so the shared statute prefix never matched (6 962 cached of 1.57 M tokens on 6 Sep); the OpenAI adapter now marks an explicit breakpoint after the statute block (settled-call cache 99-100 percent in pre-flight). Because the schema on the wire changed for every model, every decide cell is re-run so that the paper's rows come from one configuration. Pre-flight (tools/preflight.py): 2 cells + 1 settled cell per model checked for parse, refusal and cache read before the grid continues.

Per-case-balanced 54-scenario suite (6 x 3/3/3, gold approved 2026-09-06), main 98e9911: English official-translation corpus, Ruling H statute units, Ruling I stage 2 over every rule, Ruling J single-call decide with justification on every row, Ruling K prompt ids. Supersedes the 2026-09-0[1-4] run of the same condition (47-scenario suite, retired ids). Calibration 20260906-llm-only-calibration: 54 gpt-5-mini calls EUR 0.20, cached share 0.82, ~1 050 output tokens per decide call.

condition.notes: The architecture minus the solver. Same claim extraction as `architecture`; the decision step is an LLM given the solver's inputs. Difference to `architecture` = the value of a deterministic decider; difference to llm-decides-on-oracle-inputs-full-procedure = the error contributed by LLM grounding.
